children: WALL STREET WEAKENS AFTER FED HIKE, WARSH PRESSER
Wall Street's main indexes closed lower on Wednesday, although the Nasdaq
finished barely red, after the Federal Reserve's announcement of a 25-basis-point increase in overnight interest rates.
Along with the rate increase, the Fed signaled that it could follow up with more increases in borrowing costs in coming months.

New Fed chief Kevin Warsh joined a unanimous decision to hike rates. Meanwhile, new policy projections, otherwise known as the dot plot, showed that 16 out of 18 policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter-percentage-point hike by the end of this year, with only two of them seeing rates remaining stable from here. Warsh did not submit a rate projection.
Stocks held more or less steady after the Fed's statement and before Warsh's press conference. But after he started talking the indexes lost some steam.

"There were expectations that you were going to get a rate hike, which we got. The issue from an equities standpoint, and the reason things are weaker is because Chair Warsh was pretty vague with a lack of specifics and a lack of real content in the press conference," said Michael James, managing director of equity sales trading at Rosenblatt Securities in Los Angeles.

"He answered all the questions with the right buzzwords but a lot of it was from a 30,000-foot view. The market wanted to get a better sense of after this rate hike, what should we be expecting going forward," said James. "That's indicative of the increased frustration from a lot of portfolio managers over Chair Warsh's style of communication."
The U.S. dollar
rallied after the hike and the 10-year Treasury yield
went from a decline to a slight gain by the time the stock market had closed.
Ahead of the Fed statement most of the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors were still gaining, but by the end of the day, most finished in the red with more cyclical groups taking the biggest hits.
Energy
slid 3% as oil prices settled down with Brent
dipping 2.7% and U.S. crude
falling 3.1% after reports that Saudi Arabia was offering additional crude cargoes through Oman while a smaller-than-expected draw in U.S. crude inventories added further downward pressure.
Just tech
, healthcare
and utilities
eked out higher closes.
Beneath the surface, both the Nasdaq Biotechnology Index
and the PHLX Semiconductor Index
ended modestly higher.
Here is a snapshot of where markets stood shortly after 4 p.m. ET:
Nasdaq closes down just 0.01%, S&P 500 falls ~0.5%, Dow down >1%
Energy is weakest S&P 500 sector; tech, with small rise, leads gainers
US Fed hikes rates by 25 basis points, dot plot indicates more to come
Dollar on track for biggest daily gain in 3 months; bitcoin up slightly; gold dips; US crude falls >3%
US 10-year Treasury yield edges up to ~5.02%
